traps.title: button vs div[role=button]
traps.trick: Same accessible role+name and identical box, but one is a real <button> with disabled and the other a div with role=button, tabIndex, aria-disabled and a manual Enter/Space keydown. Extra onKeyDown handler and a different tag must not hide the duplicate.

traps.title: aria-label vs visually-hidden text
traps.trick: Identical icon button; the accessible name 'Close dialog' comes from aria-label on canon and from an extra <span class=sr-only> on app. Same announced name, different DOM (one extra span).

traps.title: aria-labelledby vs aria-label+title
traps.trick: Same region landmark named 'Billing'. Canon uses aria-labelledby -> its own h2#id; app uses aria-label plus a redundant title and drops the id, and factors the two definition rows into a local wrapper. Same landmark, same name, different naming mechanism.

traps.title: identical pixels, different announcement
traps.trick: NEGATIVE. Pixel-identical to NavToggle, but announces 'Collapse sidebar' instead of 'Open navigation menu', uses toggle semantics (aria-pressed) instead of disclosure (aria-expanded + aria-controls), exposes the glyph as a named img instead of aria-hidden, adds a role=presentation wrapper, and tabIndex=-1 removes it from the tab order. Looks the same to a reader, is a different control to a screen reader.

traps.title: a11y contract buried 5 wrappers deep
traps.trick: Same ARIA menu (role=menu + aria-label on the list, role=none on li, role=menuitem + tabIndex=-1 on the button). Canon spreads it across 5 chained components in 5 files; app collapses it to 3 levels in 3 files with entirely different names. The a11y attributes live 3-5 components below the exported entry point.

traps.title: tailwind vs styled-components, same CSS
traps.trick: Identical final CSS on a price pill reached by two routes: canon uses tailwind arbitrary-value utilities, app uses a styled-components template with shorthand padding and numeric font-weight. Requires real tailwind v4 resolution plus styled template parsing to see they are the same.

traps.title: tailwind base overridden by styled, vs resolved inline
traps.trick: Override chain. Canon writes misleading tailwind utilities (4px radius, 8px padding, indigo background) on a styled.section whose template overrides radius/padding/background to 12px/24px/#ffffff; the tailwind border survives because styled never sets it. App writes the already-resolved CSS straight into style={{...}}. Only the RESOLVED styles match.

traps.title: styled base overridden by inline, vs tailwind
traps.trick: Second override chain, opposite direction. Canon's styled chip is grey (#e2e8f0/#334155) but an inline style overrides it to the green resolved palette; app expresses that same resolved green directly as tailwind utilities. Both carry the same onClick and dot span.

traps.title: same layout, different color/cursor/behavior
traps.trick: NEGATIVE. Same height, padding, radius, gap, font-size and font-weight as SortHeader, but it is a static caption: slate text instead of indigo, cursor-default instead of cursor-pointer, a span instead of a button, no onClick, no aria-pressed and no chevron. Layout matches; typography, color, cursor and behavior do not.

traps.title: top/left vs inset shorthand
traps.trick: Same absolutely-positioned notification badge. Canon uses left-[16px] top-[12px]; app uses the inset shorthand inset-[12px_auto_auto_16px]. Requires normalizing inset into per-side offsets to see the same position.

traps.title: 6 wrappers vs 7 different wrappers, same tree
traps.trick: Both chains are cross-file and fully local. Canon: Frame > Row > Body > Title/Text plus a Glyph leaf (6 components). App: Shell > Lead > Inner > Copy > Headline/Paragraph plus an Accent leaf (7 components), where BannerCopy is a fragment-only pass-through that emits no DOM. Different names, different grouping, different depth, identical expanded tree.

traps.title: 5-level wrapper chain vs raw HTML
traps.trick: Canon builds a figure/img/figcaption card through 5 local wrapper components (including next/image -> img); app renders the identical final HTML as raw elements in one component with zero wrappers. Tests wrapper expansion against a flat baseline.

traps.title: guard-clause null vs ternary undefined
traps.trick: Same empty-state tree, opposite control flow. Canon uses an early `if (messages > 0) return null` guard; app uses a single return with a ternary whose other branch is `undefined`, plus a nested ternary that yields identical text on both arms. The rendered tree is the same for every input.

traps.title: branches that genuinely change the tree
traps.trick: NEGATIVE. Same filters domain and shared chrome, and both switch on an open/expanded flag, but the branches really differ: fieldset/legend with two checkboxes and a single Apply button, versus div[role=region] with an h3, three checkboxes and an extra Reset button in a flex row. Different structure, different a11y, different behavior.

traps.title: FLAGSHIP: 34-file feature tree vs 8-file styled primitives
traps.trick: A realistic project-overview page (sticky header with brand/nav/search/bell/avatar, 8 KPI tiles, 8 task rows with checkbox+priority+status, 3 milestone cards with progressbars and next/image, invite form, activity feed, team roster, footer). Canon decomposes by feature across 33 files and up to 6 nesting levels; app decomposes by element kind into 62 styled primitives plus flat data-driven sections in 8 files, using `as={Link}` polymorphism and a single generic tile renderer instead of 8 tile components. No shared component names. Both expand to the SAME 233-line HTML tree.

traps.title: onEdit/onPress vs onChange/onClick + spread props
traps.trick: Same newsletter form and same final HTML. Canon passes handlers as onEdit/onPress with inline JSX props and an inline arrow submit; app builds spread prop objects in a different key order, uses a named change arrow and a named submit function, and names the leaf props conventionally (onChange/onClick, plus loading+disabled). Handler plumbing and prop order differ; behavior and tree do not.

traps.title: media transport vs pagination bar
traps.trick: NEGATIVE. Same bar chrome, same lucide-icon-in-round-button vocabulary and same onClick/onChange wiring as TransportControls, but it is pagination: nav instead of div[role=group], next/link anchors instead of buttons, a page counter instead of a play/pause toggle, and a select instead of a range input. Shares framework signals and layout, is a different component.

traps.title: KPI tile vs author card
traps.trick: NEGATIVE. Identical article shell, width, border, radius, padding, gap and type scale, and both use the same framework imports vocabulary, but the contents differ: a metric with a trend delta versus an avatar image, a two-line bio and a next/link profile anchor. Superficially the same card, semantically a different one.
